text: Triage on the reported controller limit breach — shrinking the case to isolate the cause.
Shrink isolated a minimal failure at step one — now verifying reproducibility and capturing state details.
The captured state shows the force spiking past its cap — testing a counterfactual tweak to confirm the cause.
The noise-free run passed when theory suggested it should still exceed the limit — digging into the exact numbers to understand why.

citations.claim: initial state has zero controller force and zero speed, so violation is not initial condition
first violating step: controller_force 144.736 exceeds fmax 111.335

counterfactual.change: Set controller noise from 0.2090759 to 0.0, keeping all other fields identical. With noise disabled the controller force is correctly clamped to fmax (111.335) and no violation occurs, showing noise handling bypasses the force limit.

args.explanation: Shrunk scenario shows controller_force 144.74 > fmax 111.33 at step 1 when noise=0.209. With noise=0 the same kp/vcmd/waypoint yields exactly fmax (clamped). Likely cause: controller computes force as kp * (vcmd direction + noise) or adds noise after clamping / computes error from noisy measurement but fails to clamp the resulting force, so noisy velocity error drives commanded force beyond fmax.

args.explanation: Shrunk scenario has controller noise=0.209 and kp=25.9, vcmd=13.43. At step 1 controller_force=144.736 exceeds fmax=111.335. With identical scenario but noise=0, force is clamped to exactly fmax (111.335) and no violation. Likely cause: noise is added to sensor/velocity-error after or instead of inside the clamp, so noisy command bypasses fmax limiting.

description: Both tiles show the red controller-driven body near the top-right corner far from the green waypoint in the bottom-left, with almost no displacement between step 0 and step 1. No wall contact, overlap, or other bodies are visible and no dramatic motion occurs.
